    If you need to change this part

    Serve another completed model run

    From the project root in PowerShell, assign the intended completed run's relative path to $selectedRun. Set $demoName = 'code-guide-' + (Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss'), then run uv run --frozen python scripts/prepare_demo.py --results-dir "$selectedRun" --output-dir "data/demo/$demoName". Set $env:KIDNEY_BIOPSY_RESULTS_DIR = $selectedRun and $env:KIDNEY_BIOPSY_DEMO_DIR = "data/demo/$demoName" in the service's PowerShell session before restarting it. Verify /health and /model, compare a prediction with the CLI configured for that same run, and reload open browser pages. For a container, pass the same paths as --results-dir and --demo-dir to prepare_container.py; its launcher uses the bundle's selection.

    Increase the interactive upload limit

    Change MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES or MAX_SPECIMENS in api.py, then update /model consumers, browser messages, API documentation, and the size/row boundary tests. The browser currently contains literal 2 MiB text in more than one place. Keep streamed byte enforcement; changing only Content-Length checks leaves incomplete enforcement. CLI limits are independent.

    Change normalization or accepted targets

    Start in the shared preprocessing code and schema, not in the route or browser. The model was fitted against a particular normalized feature definition. Produce a new compatible run, preserve the old run, and verify raw-count predictions agree across direct, CLI, HTTP, and walkthrough paths.

    Change the result presentation

    Keep identity checks before rendering and clear prior results on input changes. Show server-provided flags, retain full values for comparison, and round only display text. Review one specimen, multiple specimens, rejected input, missing walkthrough evidence, and a page left open while the served model changes.

    Check your understanding

    Why can /health return 503 even though the page opens?

    Serving the HTML page does not require a loaded model. The lifespan startup must successfully verify and load the configured Predictor before /health reports ready. Inspect the startup category and configured artifacts, then restart after repair.

    A public example still scores after changing models, but its walkthrough fails. Is that contradictory?

    No. Its raw counts may satisfy the new model's schema, so ordinary scoring can succeed. The prepared explanation also asserts a model identity; a mismatch prevents that explanation from being attached to the new prediction. Prepare examples for the new model and reload the page.

    A score displays as 0.877 beside a threshold displayed as 0.876588. Which values determine the flag?

    The server compares the full model score with the full frozen threshold using >=. Rounded browser text is for reading only. The browser renders the returned flag rather than calculating a new decision from formatted numbers.

    Why does a valid 17-specimen CSV work in the CLI but fail in the browser service?

    They share scientific preprocessing and prediction, but have different operational limits. The API accepts at most 16 specimens and 2 MiB; the CLI CSV path accepts at most 1,000 specimens and 20 MiB. This is a transport contract difference, not a different model calculation.

    Would calling predict_normalized with raw counts work if the columns have the correct names?

    It could pass some structural checks and still give invalid results because the model expects normalized values. That method trusts the caller to have normalized the data. Application callers must use Predictor.predict so the shared transformation always runs.

    06

    Reproduce and maintain the project

    Choose the right check for the change, preserve completed evidence, and package the same trusted model for local serving.

    Understanding the checks means knowing what a passing result actually establishes. Fast tests use generated fixtures and check software behavior. A reproduction check compares saved experiment outputs. The real HTTP check compares all 345 validation specimens through the saved results, command line, and running API. The container check verifies the packaged model, page, examples, and displayed evidence.

    The service's default run is results/reproduction/20260915_shared. Later research runs do not automatically replace it. A serving bundle copies the selected model, its original manifests and metadata, evaluation counts, and prepared examples while preserving their relative paths. It is a small project root that starts without raw training files or another model fit.

    The GitHub Actions workflow installs the locked package, runs lint, formatting, and tests, then builds and checks an image using a tiny model labeled synthetic-ci-only. That establishes packaging behavior without a full research run. Its synthetic predictions are not classifier-performance evidence. Local research-container records and the dated hosted CI pass describe the specific code and artifacts checked; a cloud deployment has not been performed.

    Follow GSM6510425. The prepared CSV has its own recorded hash. The container verifier can send it to the service and compare its score, flag, threshold, and model version with the locally loaded predictor.

    Critical functions

    Run fast checks and save evidence for this revisionmain · scripts/check_project.py

    Check the local Python package and test suite without downloading public data or requiring the fitted research model.

    Receives
    The repository source, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, the project's Python 3.12 environment, and optional --require-installed and --output arguments.
    Returns or writes
    A JSON software-check record, test output in the terminal, and an exit status suitable for CI. The command creates a timestamped path by default.

    What happens, and in what order

    1. Choose a new evidence path, then record hashes for active Python source, project configuration, lockfile, workflow, and page assets. Existing check records cannot be overwritten.
    2. Compile source in memory and parse both TOML files. Call check_environment to require Python 3.12, an environment inside this project, and a package import from this project. With --require-installed, the package must come from the environment rather than editable source.
    3. Check that packaged HTML, CSS, and JavaScript assets exist and match the working source. This catches a wheel that imports successfully but omits or ships stale web assets.
    4. Discover and run the unittest suite. Save test counts, failures, package versions, source hashes, elapsed time, and success status in a new JSON record; return a nonzero exit status when checks fail.

    Why this design: A pass tied to source hashes is more useful than a floating test count in documentation. The installed-package mode catches packaging problems that editable development imports can hide. Generated test inputs keep routine checks fast and independent of private or downloaded specimens.

    When it fails: The wrong Python version, an environment or imported package outside this project, missing/stale installed page assets, invalid syntax/TOML, and test failures make the record unsuccessful. Lint and formatting are separate commands in the workflow, not hidden steps inside this function.

    If you change it: After changing source, run lint, formatting checks, and this command. If source assets changed after a noneditable installation, reinstall the current package before testing installed-package behavior. Do not cite an earlier record as verification of the new source.

    Determine whether a fixed training procedure was reproducedmain · scripts/verify_reproduction.py

    Compare a new completed run with the preserved baseline at the specimen, model-selection, threshold, and split levels.

    Receives
    Two completed run directories, each with its manifest, prediction tables, frozen metadata, and saved split, plus a new JSON output path. The default reference is results/reproduction/baseline; --run-dir and --output are required.
    Returns or writes
    A preservation/reproduction JSON record identifying both runs and the compared prediction tables. A successful result means the checked outputs agree within the stated tolerance.

    What happens, and in what order

    1. Call verify_artifacts on both runs to check each artifact's recorded size and SHA-256. This check compares existing outputs; it does not run training itself.
    2. For every reference prediction CSV, require unique matching specimen IDs, reorder the new table to the reference, and compare labels and flags exactly. Require finite absolute score differences no larger than 1e-12.
    3. Compare every reference frozen record's selected model, threshold, ordered features, and train/screen/test counts. Separately compare the complete saved split table after sorting by specimen.
    4. Write the run identities, manifest hashes, artifact counts, score tolerance, selected thresholds, and per-table maximum differences to a new evidence file.

    Why this design: A refactor can pass small tests yet change actual results. Comparing every saved specimen catches changes that a rounded aggregate score could conceal. Distinguish the training command from this comparison: checking two previously saved runs is not evidence that a new fit just occurred.

    When it fails: Changed artifact bytes, missing tables, unequal specimen sets, changed labels or flags, score differences beyond tolerance, changed thresholds/features/model selection, or changed split assignments fail the comparison.

    If you change it: Use this check after a fixed-procedure rerun. If a method intentionally changes, preserve the new run and explain the result as a new experiment or follow-up; do not loosen tolerance or rewrite the baseline simply to get a pass. Current-source differences alone do not mean historical artifacts should be edited.

    Verified public raw files, a configured completed run, a new aggregate-output directory, and a new case directory under ignored data/processed. Its default run matches the frozen service run.
    Returns or writes
    An aggregate http.json record with agreement measures and source hashes; CLI/HTTP specimen CSVs and the server log stay in the ignored case directory. The temporary server is stopped.

    What happens, and in what order

    1. Verify the public inputs and selected saved prediction table, load the configured predictor, and read all validation specimens from the source files. Require exact agreement between validation IDs and saved prediction IDs.
    2. Invoke the installed CLI in a subprocess to generate an independent prediction CSV. Start Uvicorn on an available localhost port using the same configured run, wait for readiness, and check model identity and HTML serving.
    3. Send counts in batches of 16 with target columns reversed. Compare every returned score to CLI and saved values within 1e-12; require identical flags, exact thresholds, one model version, and passed input checks.
    4. Send an incomplete batch missing IFNG and a 17-specimen batch. Require a whole-batch rejection without predictions. Save aggregate evidence and ignored specimen outputs, then stop the server in a finally block, including on failures.

    Why this design: The in-process API tests are useful but do not test a real socket, server startup, installed command execution, or every saved research prediction. Reversing target columns verifies name-based input matching across the complete serving path.

    When it fails: Missing or altered inputs, an unready server, the wrong model, mismatched specimens/scores/flags, incorrect batch limits, or partial predictions for invalid input raise errors. Only successful completion writes http.json; a partial directory is not a passing record.

    If you change it: Run this after a meaningful change to parsing, preprocessing, model loading, CLI defaults, or API prediction behavior. A deliberate batch-limit change also requires updating this verifier's fixed 16/17-specimen checks and the documented API contract.

    • ApiTests.test_batch_limit_is_applied_before_returning_results — Protects whole-batch rejection before the slower real-data HTTP check.

    Copy exactly the files needed to serve one selected modelprepare_bundle · scripts/prepare_container.py

    Create a new self-contained serving bundle from trusted project artifacts without modifying the original experiment or copying raw training data.

    Receives
    A project root, selected run directory, prepared demo directory, and new output directory. Defaults select the frozen shared run, data/demo, and build/container.
    Returns or writes
    A small project-root directory containing the trusted model, original run/frozen/result records, demo manifest and CSVs, and bundle.json. The original run manifest can still mention research artifacts that were deliberately not copied.

    What happens, and in what order

    1. Require normalized project-relative paths, a new destination, and no case-insensitive copy-path collisions. Read the original run manifest and require a unique artifact entry for the selected model, frozen metadata, and evaluation results.
    2. Verify required artifact hashes and load the model through the shared load_predictor. Check that the evaluation's selected model and threshold match the frozen predictor; agreement of hashes alone is not enough for semantic compatibility.
    3. Read the demo manifest and require the same run and model version. Verify example hashes, safe unique IDs, descriptions, CSV paths, and file sizes. Parse every example with the frozen schema and verify that its declared valid/invalid status is true. Score valid examples and require at least one valid and one invalid example.
    4. Only after input verification, create the destination and physically copy the selected files while retaining their relative paths. Recheck copied bytes and load the predictor from the copied root.
    5. Write bundle.json last with run/demo paths, model/schema identity, and the copied-file records. This completion record is absent if copying stops before the bundle is ready.

    Why this design: Training and serving have different file needs. A narrow verified bundle makes the Docker image independent of raw downloads and unrelated models while keeping the exact recorded paths and artifact hashes. The configured model is trusted project code/data, never an API caller's upload; joblib loading is not a safe parser for arbitrary untrusted model files.

    When it fails: Existing destinations, unsafe or colliding paths, missing/tampered artifacts, incompatible schema, changed evaluation threshold, wrong demo model, inaccurate validity labels, and incomplete examples fail preparation. Source checks happen before output creation; a copy failure can leave an incomplete destination without bundle.json.

    If you change it: To switch models, prepare examples for the intended completed run and create a fresh bundle for that same run. Rebuilding the application image alone does not select a newer research run. Do not edit hashes to make incompatible files appear consistent; investigate the changed artifact and regenerate the intended bundle.

    Checks to understand

    • ContainerBundleTests.test_bundle_serves_same_model_and_examples_without_source_data — Proves serving works from copied files alone and leaves source files unchanged.
    • ContainerBundleTests.test_evaluation_threshold_must_match_even_when_hashes_are_updated — A matching hash does not excuse incompatible result metadata.
    • ContainerBundleTests.test_existing_bundle_is_preserved — An existing serving selection cannot be silently overwritten.

    Start the API from the model selected at image build timemain · scripts/serve_container.py

    Translate the bundled selection into service configuration and launch one API process inside the image.

    Receives
    runtime/bundle.json beside the installed launcher and the serving files copied there by the Dockerfile. This layout is created during image construction.
    Returns or writes
    A running Uvicorn service using the image's selected model and examples. The Dockerfile installs locked dependencies, supplies an unprivileged user, and defines a readiness command against /health.

    What happens, and in what order

    1. Resolve the runtime directory relative to the launcher's own location and read its completion record. Require bundle format version 1.
    2. Set KIDNEY_BIOPSY_PROJECT_ROOT, KIDNEY_BIOPSY_RESULTS_DIR, and KIDNEY_BIOPSY_DEMO_DIR from that bundled selection before importing the ASGI application through Uvicorn.
    3. Start kidney_biopsy.api:app on container port 8000 with access logs disabled. The API's startup path loads and verifies the configured model; this launcher does not fit a model or fetch inputs.

    Why this design: The image should serve a known artifact even if the development machine later creates new runs. Configuration comes from the prepared bundle, and the HTTP caller cannot choose a model path. Listening on all container interfaces allows the host to publish the port; local demonstration commands bind the host side to 127.0.0.1.

    When it fails: Missing/malformed completion metadata or an unsupported bundle version prevents launch. A model that fails API startup checks remains unready rather than becoming a usable predictor. Docker availability and host port binding are separate environment concerns.

    If you change it: If the bundle layout or format changes, update preparation, launcher, Dockerfile, and verification together. Check the rebuilt image's readiness and predictions. The image uses a maintained Python base tag, so identical project source alone does not guarantee identical image bytes; the container record identifies the actual checked image.

    Verify what the packaged application actually servescheck_service · scripts/verify_container.py

    Compare the running HTTP service with the trusted local serving bundle, including numerical results and displayed explanations.

    Receives
    An HTTP-compatible client, the verified local bundle root, and parsed bundle metadata. The script's main verifies bundle file hashes and waits for readiness before calling this function.
    Returns or writes
    Aggregate verification results describing valid specimens, invalid examples, walkthroughs, maximum score difference, and agreement of assets, metadata, example files, and evaluation counts. The outer script writes the dated JSON evidence.

    What happens, and in what order

    1. Load the local predictor and compare /model with its model version, schema/preprocessing versions, threshold, and required targets. Reconstruct expected evaluation counts from the bundled research results and compare the displayed values.
    2. Check that the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript are served with nonempty content and expected content types. Compare the public example listing and each downloaded CSV byte-for-byte with the bundle.
    3. For each valid example, parse the local source, reverse its target columns, submit it to /predict, and compare the full prediction table with local inference within 1e-12. For invalid examples, require HTTP 422 with a structured invalid_csv error and no traceback.
    4. When an example has a recorded diagnosis, request its walkthrough and call check_walkthrough. That check reconstructs the IFNG normalization, all housekeeping values, model identity, and prediction from the actual source specimen rather than trusting displayed arithmetic.
    5. Return aggregate counts and agreement measures. The outer main can start a temporary image with a read-only filesystem, verify its Docker readiness command, record image identity and elapsed time, and remove the container even on failure. It also accepts an already running URL.

    Why this design: A green health endpoint only says a model loaded. This check catches serving the wrong model, incorrect displayed counts, stale example files, or a convincing but wrong walkthrough. The same path tests the synthetic CI image and the actual research image, while their evidence keeps those purposes distinct.

    When it fails: A changed score fails even when the declared model version is unchanged. Missing assets, wrong thresholds/metadata, altered example bytes, incorrect walkthrough arithmetic, or invalid input accepted as valid also fail. The outer script records failure and exits nonzero; a record file's existence alone does not mean success.

    If you change it: After a packaging or demo change, rebuild a fresh image and run the checker against the intended bundle. If a displayed field is added, update its expected-value check where it affects the user's interpretation. A successful local image check does not establish a cloud deployment.

    If you need to change this part

    Check a routine software change

    From the project root, run uv sync --frozen, uv run --no-sync ruff check src scripts tests experiments, uv run --no-sync ruff format --check src scripts tests experiments, then uv run --no-sync python scripts/check_project.py. The last command automatically chooses a new evidence path. These commands check software behavior; they do not rerun research training.

    Rerun the fixed experiment and verify its predictions

    First run uv run --frozen python experiments/rejection_public/download.py and uv run --frozen python scripts/verify_local_data.py; existing valid local inputs are reused. In PowerShell set $runName = 'code-guide-' + (Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss'). Run uv run --frozen python experiments/rejection_public/run.py --output-dir "results/reproduction/$runName" --model-dir "data/processed/models/$runName", then uv run --frozen python scripts/verify_reproduction.py --run-dir "results/reproduction/$runName" --output "results/checks/$runName/reproduction.json". This is the full fixed training procedure, followed by comparison; preserve both old and new runs.

    Verify the real service after a prediction-path change

    Set $checkName = 'code-guide-' + (Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss'), then run uv run --frozen python scripts/verify_http_service.py --output-dir "results/checks/$checkName/http" --case-dir "data/processed/application_checks/$checkName". It starts and stops its own local server and checks all 345 frozen validation predictions. See docs/VERIFICATION.md for the separate installed-package and fresh-environment checks.

    Build a new image without replacing an existing bundle

    With the default frozen model and prepared examples available, set $bundleName = 'code-guide-' + (Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss'), then run uv run --frozen python scripts/prepare_container.py --output-dir "build/container/$bundleName". With a running Linux Docker engine, run docker build --platform linux/amd64 --build-arg "BUNDLE_DIR=build/container/$bundleName" --tag "kidney-biopsy:$bundleName" ., then uv run --frozen python scripts/verify_container.py --image "kidney-biopsy:$bundleName" --bundle-dir "build/container/$bundleName" --output "results/checks/$bundleName/container.json". Fresh names preserve earlier bundles, images, and records; the temporary verification container is removed.

    Check your understanding

    The research script finished a better-looking new run. Why is the app still serving the old model?

    Research output does not automatically change the serving selection. The default is results/reproduction/20260915_shared; an image gets its selection from bundle.json. Prepare compatible examples and a new bundle for the intended run, configure or rebuild the service, and verify the resulting model version, scores, and threshold.

    CI passed with the synthetic model. What remains to check before saying the current research application reproduces the saved results?

    The synthetic fixture checks software and packaging. Run the real HTTP verifier against the selected local research run and the container verifier against its real bundle. If training or learned transformations changed, also create a new fixed-procedure run and compare its outputs. Do not use synthetic fixture accuracy as evidence about biopsies.

    A model file's hash no longer matches. Is updating the manifest a repair?

    No. First determine why the bytes changed and which model belongs to the intended run. Preserve historical records and recover the original verified artifact or make a new completed run and bundle. Hashes detect disagreement with trusted records; they do not make an incompatible or untrusted model valid.

    Which check catches a page showing the correct model version but different numerical scores?

    check_service compares actual HTTP predictions with the local bundled predictor. ContainerVerificationTests.test_changed_scores_fail_even_when_version_metadata_agrees deliberately changes a model's scores while retaining its version and requires the checker to fail.

    07

    Source & maintenance

    The explanations are hand-written; the source excerpts, symbol links, and file hashes are checked during the build.

    The diagrams deliberately show the important calls and artifact transfers, rather than every helper or import. A module can appear in several workflows because its responsibilities are shared. Historical copies under results/ preserve earlier experiments; the active implementation is under src/, experiments/, and scripts/.

    Each function's source link opens the corresponding embedded file at its recorded line. Links labeled “Open current local file” and the related documentation links require the surrounding checkout. Diagram links, explanations, tests, search, and print work in the standalone file.

    Update this guide after changing code

    1. Edit the chapter JSON under docs/code_guide/. Update the workflow relationships in diagrams.json if calls or saved files change.
    2. Run uv run --frozen python scripts/build_code_guide.py from the project root. The builder rejects missing symbols, missing files, broken anchors, and diagram nodes without explanations.
    3. If preprocessing, prediction, or walkthrough code changed, use uv run --frozen python scripts/build_code_guide.py --refresh-example to recalculate the public example with the project-controlled frozen model. A normal build needs no model or raw assay files.
    4. Review changed explanations against the source. The build checks references and captures hashes; it cannot determine whether prose still explains the implementation correctly.
    5. Run uv run --frozen python scripts/build_code_guide.py --check, then open the HTML and inspect the affected diagrams and links. Commit the editable sources, generated HTML, and docs/code_guide/build_manifest.json together.

    Scope of the source record

    The latest commit affecting the documented source at build time was a666922b172a349ad1775312d94f4f66a5117040; working source differs from HEAD. Exact input hashes are recorded in build_manifest.json. The public specimen record identifies its model run, prepared CSV hash, and calculation source hashes. Existing model results and verification reports are historical evidence; building this guide is not a new training run or a rerun of those software checks.

    1"""Explain one prepared public specimen using the service's actual preprocessing."""23from __future__ import annotations45import numpy as np6import pandas as pd78from .prediction import Predictor9from .preprocessing import DIAGNOSES, normalize_counts101112def describe_specimen(counts: pd.DataFrame, item: dict, predictor: Predictor) -> dict:13    """Keep public labels separate from the measurements passed to the model."""14    if len(counts) != 1 or counts.index[0] != item.get("specimen"):15        raise ValueError("Walkthrough specimen differs from the prepared example.")16    diagnosis = item.get("recorded_diagnosis")17    if diagnosis not in DIAGNOSES:18        raise ValueError("Walkthrough needs a known recorded diagnosis.")19    if item.get("model_version") != predictor.model_version:20        raise ValueError("Prepared example model differs from the configured model.")21    if "IFNG" not in predictor.schema.features:22        raise ValueError("Walkthrough needs the IFNG assay target.")2324    # Use the same transformation as prediction; the displayed arithmetic only25    # explains one target. The entire ordered panel is passed to the fitted model.26    normalized = normalize_counts(counts, predictor.schema)27    log_counts = np.log2(counts.astype(float) + 1).iloc[0]28    housekeeping = [29        {30            "target": target,31            "raw_count": float(counts.iloc[0][target]),32            "log2_count_plus_one": float(log_counts[target]),33        }34        for target in predictor.schema.housekeeping_targets35    ]36    prediction = predictor.predict_normalized(normalized).to_dict(orient="records")[0]37    return {38        "example_id": item["id"],39        "specimen": item["specimen"],40        "recorded_diagnosis": diagnosis,41        "recorded_rejection": bool(DIAGNOSES[diagnosis]),42        "model_version": predictor.model_version,43        "schema_version": predictor.schema.schema_version,44        "preprocessing_version": predictor.schema.preprocessing_version,45        "threshold": predictor.threshold,46        "required_targets": len(predictor.schema.required_targets),47        "predictor_targets": len(predictor.schema.features),48        "normalization": {49            "illustrated_target": "IFNG",50            "raw_count": float(counts.iloc[0]["IFNG"]),51            "log2_count_plus_one": float(log_counts["IFNG"]),52            "housekeeping_mean": float(53                log_counts[list(predictor.schema.housekeeping_targets)].mean()54            ),55            "normalized_value": float(normalized.iloc[0]["IFNG"]),56            "housekeeping": housekeeping,57        },58        "prediction": prediction,59    }
